Handing strong low-margin top1 candidates from D1 into D2 contract evaluation revived probe12 lockbox quality to 16 trades, 56.25 percent win rate, and +1.14 percent avgNetRet while reducing false-positive rejections from 56 to 15. Probe38 and probe149 were essentially unchanged, so this looks targeted rather than globally destabilizing.

A narrow liquidity strong-candidate bypass (liquidityRatio >= 0.5, avgTradingValue20d >= 2.0B KRW, scoreMargin >= 0.003, finalScore >= 0.8) removed the last probe12 liquidity blocked-hit without opening probe38 or probe149. Probe12 Step E improved from 16 trades, 56.25 percent win rate, and +17.79 percent cumulativeReturn to 17 trades, 58.82 percent win rate, and +26.98 percent cumulativeReturn, while blocked-hit days fell from 2 to 1.

A conservative false-positive strong-candidate bypass was tested twice. The first overlay path was a no-op because the config was written to the wrong namespace. After correcting the namespace, the bypass still did not improve probe12 Step D eval and caused a severe Step E regression, so this path is not promotable.

Disabling onlineLearning together with generalization collapsed the eval split and made the run incomparable against the accepted metrics, so this experiment should not be used for promotion decisions.
Disabling onlineLearning only preserved the eval split but did not improve probe12 Step D or Step E. The top1 eval counts and blocked-hit mix remained unchanged.
Enabling conservative agreement rerank applied on a few days but did not improve probe12 Step D eval metrics and collapsed Step E to 1 losing trade, so this is not a promotable recovery path.

Goal evaluation was shifted from legacy winRate/PnL-first semantics to TARGET-first overlap semantics. Step E gate now prioritizes target hit metrics, single-position gating is disabled, tradeQualityPrior no longer rewards generic positive timeout memory, audit rows carry goal/semantics tags, and legacy experiment rows were isolated with row-level scope tagging.

A narrow top1 micro-correction that promoted top2/3 candidates when score gap was small and fill probability was materially higher recovered probe12 Step D hitAt1 from 0.1852 to 0.3333, but Step E collapsed to 0 trades because the rescued top1s were then shadowed by false-positive and agreement/day-type downstream vetoes.

Adding a false-positive strong-candidate bypass restricted to micro-corrected top1s did not clear the downstream blockade under conservative thresholds. Step D stayed at the improved 0.3333 hitAt1, but Step E remained fully blocked at 0 trades.

Tightening the micro-correction thresholds reduced over-application and still improved probe12 Step D hitAt1 from 0.1852 to 0.2222, but Step E was still negative at 5 trades, 20.0 percent win rate, and -1.72 percent avgNetRet, so the narrower D1 patch is not promotable either.
